results.Notes: Strongest comparisons: MA-Q-0267 and MA-Q-0263 (B3-B siblings, same discipline chapter but different operative provisions) and MA-Q-0211 from the prior bank. Materially distinct: this is the only item in the 294-question bank that turns on the 247 CMR 10.02 definition of Conviction, and the decision path is a definitional one, matching an admission to sufficient facts and a continuance without a finding against an expressly broadened regulatory term. No sibling overlap: MA-Q-0263 uses conviction only as a reporting trigger and MA-Q-0267 concerns out-of-state conduct equivalence. Tranche-level observation recorded for the controller rather than against this item: within the 20 SBA items of BATCH3-B3B the keyed position is A six times, B never, C twice, D once and E eleven times (chi-square 20.5 on 4 degrees of freedom, p of about 0.0004). The repository gate scripts/check_answer_distribution.py passes because it measures the whole 181-item SBA bank, where E was previously the least used key, so the tranche-level concentration is invisible to it. Each item's own wording remains sound, so this item passes wording_not_guessable on its own terms, but the set should be rebalanced before B3-B is used as a standalone practice block.

Strongest comparisons: MA-Q-0115 (serious event deadline) and MA-Q-0056 (serious events) from the prior bank, plus B3-B sibling MA-Q-0262. Materially distinct: no prior bank item addresses the 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) and (aa) reporting grounds, and the reasoning is a two-clock sorting task in which the unit differs (seven business days against 30 calendar days) and one trigger is a pending charge rather than a disposition. Sibling MA-Q-0262 supplies the conviction definition but not the clocks, so the two are complementary rather than overlapping.

Strongest comparisons: B3-B sibling MA-Q-0268, which is the closest pair in the tranche (composite 0.587, shared rule MA-DISCIPLINE-OUT-OF-STATE, stem cosine 0.388), and MA-Q-0253 from the prior bank. Sibling overlap is present and deliberate, and it resolves: this item tests the conduct-equivalence gate in 247 CMR 10.06(7), while MA-Q-0268 tests the protected-activity override in 247 CMR 10.03(3). The stem here expressly stipulates that the conduct is not covered by any statutory protection, which forecloses the MA-Q-0268 path and keeps the two decision paths separate. Both reach a negative outcome by different routes, which is acceptable but is the item pairing the controller should watch if further out-of-state items are authored.

The inpatient carve-out proposition is scope-of-exclusion reasoning rather than recall.

Strongest comparisons: prior-bank MA-Q-0162 (federal corresponding responsibility under the 21 CFR 1306.04 doctrine) and MA-Q-0104. Distinct from the bank: MA-Q-0162 is a federal single-best-answer item about resolving red flags, whereas this is a Massachusetts item enumerating the four conjunctive determinations in 247 CMR 9.15(2), so distinct_from_bank is satisfied. REALISM FAIL on authentic_distractors. Under the canonical key A, C, D and E, the only incorrect option is B, that the patient has no outstanding account balance with the pharmacy, which has no regulatory nexus to 247 CMR 9.15(2) and which no prepared candidate would credit; the entire discriminating power of the item therefore rests on a single inauthentic distractor. The defect is compounded by the stem, which asks which determinations the pharmacist must still make after the prescriber has confirmed authorship over the telephone. That wording supports a reasonable reading on which determination (c) has been discharged and the answer is A, C and E; that is the answer I recorded in the Phase-1 blind lock before any canonical content was unsealed, and it is the only one of 33 items where my blind answer diverged from the key. The key is legally correct and the legal record verdict is KEEP with Existing_Answer_Correct YES, because 247 CMR 9.15(2) is conjunctive and the telephone call is evidence going to authenticity rather than a dispensation from determining it. The remedy is item construction, not law: replace option B with a legally plausible but incorrect determination, and either delete still from the stem or restate it so that the enumerative reading is unambiguous. Recorded as MINOR_EDIT, Severity Medium.

The trap, that an institutional account does not discharge a personally imposed duty, is a realistic staffing scenario and does not arise in either reporting item.

Strongest comparisons: prior-bank MA-Q-0138 (PTT ADD eligibility) and MA-Q-0025, and B3-B sibling MA-Q-0290. Strongest comparison: prior-bank MA-Q-0081, which enumerates the general statutory CDTM qualifications under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b), including the $1,000,000 insurance figure and the five additional CE contact hours. This item is materially distinct because it asks which conditions attach because prescriptive practices are included, which is the separate overlay in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f); the two incorrect numeric options are deliberate corruptions of the MA-Q-0081 figures, so the item requires holding both lists at once and is not answerable from MA-Q-0081 knowledge alone. B3-B siblings MA-Q-0293 and MA-Q-0294 cover 247 CMR 16.02(2) and (3) respectively, so the three partition 247 CMR 16.02 without overlap.

Strongest comparisons: B3-B sibling MA-Q-0294 (highest sibling similarity in the CDTM cluster) and prior-bank MA-Q-0057 (record retention) and MA-Q-0081. Materially distinct: this is the only item in the bank on 247 CMR 16.02(2), and the reasoning fixes the start of the retention clock at the date of the current agreement rather than the course date, which is the inverse of the ordinary CE retention rule in 247 CMR 4.06(1) tested by MA-Q-0260. Sibling MA-Q-0294 concerns a notification duty rather than retention, and this item's option E cross-references that duty only as a distractor.

Strongest comparisons: B3-B siblings MA-Q-0293 and MA-Q-0266, and prior-bank MA-Q-0081 and MA-Q-0084. Materially distinct: this is the only item in the bank on 247 CMR 16.02(3), and the reasoning combines two steps, that a consent agreement counts as discipline for this purpose and that the notice runs to every supervising physician rather than the one connected to the conduct. MA-Q-0266 uses a consent agreement in the surrender-terms context and MA-Q-0084 concerns the 24-hour prescription copy duty, so neither reaches the discipline notification.
